current_answer: As of 3 October 2026, reviewed public evidence does not establish a broad capability decline across popular deployed models or a confirmed Opus 5.5 capability regression. BridgeBench’s latest Opus 5.5 score is 94.2% of its launch “power” (−5.8% versus launch), inside its stated 90–110% normal-variance band; the composite includes task score, tokens, and cost and lacks published sample counts or uncertainty. LiveNerf’s latest visible progress remains a baseline-in-progress note dated 1 October, with no post-baseline comparison and an earliest possible call around 24 October. OpenAI and Anthropic reported operational status at the current check. If a familiar task fails, check its surface and status, then save and replay the same task after recovery before switching.

catalogue_card.question: Does Opus 5.5’s 94.2% score prove a decline?
catalogue_card.text: No. BridgeBench’s latest score is inside its stated 90–110% range and combines task score, token use, and cost. Its test set and sample details are private; LiveNerf has no post-baseline comparison yet.

summary: No reviewed public evidence establishes a broad decline in popular deployed models or a confirmed Opus 5.5 capability regression.
BridgeBench’s latest Opus 5.5 test, dated 2 October, is 94.2% of its launch “power” (−5.8% from launch; −9.6% from 1 October). Its board calls 90–110% normal variance and displays four tests.
BridgeBench defines power using task score, tokens, and cost. It does not disclose the actual task set, weights, sample count, or uncertainty for this result.
LiveNerf’s latest visible progress note is dated 1 October and reports 8/10 baseline days complete, with no post-baseline result. Its first possible call is around 24 October.
OpenAI and Anthropic status pages showed operational systems at the 3 October check. Status is aggregate, not a measure of answer quality.
If a familiar task fails, check its surface and status, save the task, settings, route, and output, then replay against the same baseline after recovery.
uncertainty: BridgeBench’s composite is not a capability-only measure; the board does not publish sample counts, uncertainty, or the tasks for the latest test.
LiveNerf has no post-baseline comparison and covers a limited Claude Code subscription path and frozen panel.
Provider status reports do not establish account-level access or completed-task quality.
No representative user denominator, broad repeated consumer-task series, first-party pool analytics, controlled audience pilot, or purchase evidence is available.
